👮 **Wachiman** · review of the whole pull request, at `3159fb1`: all 12 files reviewed.

3 finding(s): 1 to fix, 2 to consider; 3 on their lines. Reply in a comment's thread to answer it.

### Summary

**Batch 1 of 2.** I reviewed all 8 files in part 1 and have one finding, at "fix" severity.

**The finding:** `packetCountsFor` (`export-presets.ts:223`) sizes the moov reservation from the source's average frame rate whenever an fps cap is set. Its own docstring says it should never assume a rate below 30 fps, because screen recordings can burst above their average. A mostly static recording averages well under that, so the reservation comes out too small. The muxer then throws mid-export and the hook encodes the whole video a second time, and the file still ends up without fast start. The same undercount shrinks the reserve-bytes estimate subtracted from the Small-file budget. The fix is to use the cap itself as the rate when one is set.

This doesn't reach users yet: Small file has no UI in this PR, and `start()` doesn't yet receive real source info. It will once the next PR in the stack wires both up.

**What checks out:**
- The fit/fill framing maths and its tests.
- The composed view and how it is placed on the output canvas (the poster is taken after framing).
- Mono downmix, including the cleanup of the extra audio samples.
- The fps cap that drops frames.
- The `launch()` refactor and its single retry, including cancel during the retry and ignoring messages from the old worker.

**Not verified:** `node_modules` isn't in the checkout, so I couldn't confirm that mediabunny's error text actually matches `/maximum packet count/i`. If it doesn't, the retry never fires and the export fails with the generic error.

**Batch 2 of 2.** Part 2 covers tests and docs. I found no defects, only two optional suggestions.

**Tests:** `export-presets.test.ts` is correct. I recomputed the Small-file ladder by hand (10/25 MB at 30 s, 2, 5 and 15 min), plus the bitrates, `even`, `sizeForShortSide` and the packet counts, and every expected value matches the code. The new hook tests in `use-video-export.test.ts` match the `launch()` and retry behaviour. Their gap is that the retry is only tested on a scene with no overlays or slides, so rebuilding the transferred bitmaps is never checked, and a cancel during the relaunch isn't tested either.

**Docs:** the new backlog page and its index row follow the documentation rules, and the page is also listed in the sidebar (`astro.config.mjs`). But the page describes things from the later stacked PRs as if this code already does them: the `exportPreset` sidecar field, title suffixes per preset, the `recordingStat` size check and retry, and the sheet's warning. Neither `exportPreset` nor a `recordingStat` IPC exists in the repository yet.

If it fails: Too few packets reserved → the muxer throws → the worker posts error → the hook aborts the session and calls launch() again with fastStart false (use-video-export.ts:210-221). On a second packet error the status becomes 'error' with the generic message. If it fails: If the relaunch rejects (rasterize, createImageBitmap or recordingCreate), the .catch calls fail() only while activeRef is true, so the error is visible. A cancel during the relaunch is caught by the… Evidence: `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/use-video-export.ts:200-223`, `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/use-video-export.ts:183-193`, `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/use-video-export.ts:110-117`, `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/use-video-export.test.ts:353-405`.
